issue: Under the superseded 2009 CBP directive, must a border officer have reasonable suspicion before conducting a forensic (advanced) search of an electronic device?
provision: U.S. Const. amend. IV (border search doctrine; CBP Directive 3340-049)

sides.position: Reasonable suspicion is required before a forensic (advanced) border search of an electronic device.
No reasonable suspicion is required before a forensic (advanced) border search of an electronic device.

quote: We need not decide whether reasonable suspicion was required under the prior Directive, on which there is circuit conflict.
cite: United States v. Haitao Xiang, 67 F.4th 895 (8th Cir. 2023)
